newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-LANGER SHOWS HOW TO PLAY IN WIND AND RAIN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER SHOWS HOW TO PLAY IN WIND AND RAIN.

text.p: German Bernhard Langer, seeking back to back European Tour victories, proved the most resiliant in appalling weather to take a one-stroke lead after the third round of the Benson and Hedges International on Saturday.
Langer, winner of the Italian Open last weekend, played with masterful control for a one under par 71 and a three-round total of 207, one stroke clear of Britons Ian Woosnam and Lee Westwood.

Eduardo Romero of Argentina and Briton Darren Clarke were a stroke further back on 209 in joint fourth with 25-year-old Kalle Vainola, the only Finn on the European Tour, alone in sixth after hitting a 71.
On a course swept by gusting winds and rainstorms, only 14 of the 68 players managed better than par.

"It was pretty miserable in the rain and then the wind picked up even more on the back nine," said Langer. "The wind was gusting and changing direction and the most difficult part was on the greens, the ball was wobbling around all the time."
Langer moved alone into the lead at the par five, 533-yard 11th where his second shot ended pin high and his attempted eagle shot left him with a tap in for a birdie.
He dropped a stroke on the short 13th where a wayward tee shot missed the green and ended in the rough but pars on the remaining holes was sufficient to keep him alone in the lead.

New Zealander Greg Turner, leader through the first two days, faltered early on when he dropped two shots on the 574-yard fourth hole and then another at the ninth to fall back to six under at the turn.

He pulled one back at the 12th after a great second shot left him a comfortable birdie putt but then dropped further shots at each of the next two holes and also the 16th to end with a 77 and five strokes behind Langer.

Turner's playing partner, Retief Goosen of South Africa, started level with Langer and shared the lead with him after the first nine which they both completed in 35. But then he dropped four shots in the space of three holes, including a double bogey six at the 14th, and finished with a 76.
Lee Westwood, the 24-year-old vaunted by Woosnam as Europe's answer to American Tiger Woods because of his long hitting, returned a 70 and said afterwards he enjoys playing in the wind.

"You need the right attitude and patience and stay calm," he said. "And if you miss a green, make sure you miss it in the right place. That's why Langer is so good, there's no-one better in the wind than him."
Woosnam also had a 70 which included three birdies and just one dropped shot -- but that one on the 440-yard ninth, he said, made him furious.
"I hit a one iron as well as I could 168 yards onto the green and then three-putted it! I don't know how the putter survived to the 10th, I was fuming," he said.
After that, Woosnam changed his putting grip, moving the left hand down below the right. "It went well after that," he said.
The best round of the day, a 67, came from Frenchman Fabrice Tarnaud, who was the first man on the course and began from level par.
He hit five birdies, including a chip-in from 80 feet, and did not drop a shot. His three-round total of 211 leaves him tied in seventh place and with a tilt at the lead on Sunday.
